topics.topic: How migration closure marking is coupled to successful import commit
questions: What happens if the closure mark is written but the import transaction then fails or the process crashes before it commits?
If the closure mark is durable but the import transaction fails, is the import permanently closed on restart or may it be retried?
How is a marked migration distinguished as committed so that a failed or interrupted import cannot permanently close migration?

quotes:
An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers,
   the Customers it makes, the migration closure (M10) and its one audit entry
   (M09) in one transaction, after recording the closure in the instance
   marks (A15).

A failure during the transaction leaves no project, no Customer and no
   closure.

the instance marks are not replaced, so
   numbering continues above every number ever written (A15) and a migration
   closure is never lost: at start Registry writes the closure into the store
   when the marks hold it and the store does not, and the import stays closed
   (R0-79).
judgement.why: A failed import is required to leave no closure, yet its pre-commit mark causes startup to recreate the closure and close the import.

topics.topic: Owner-session cookie scope and attributes enforcing the browser/origin boundary
questions: What exact cookie scope and attributes enforce this rule, given that cookies are scoped by host/domain and path rather than by origin and normally ignore the port?
How is the own-origin restriction enforced, especially when another origin shares Registry's host name?
What exact cookie scope and attributes enforce the stated browser boundary, including local access that may use HTTP?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the owner-session cookie attributes and deployment rules already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Owner-session cookie attributes and deployment rules, including local HTTP support
quotes: The owner signs in with the owner credential (R0-30) and receives an owner session (M11), carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin.
precedent.why: Exact cookie attributes, host/path scope and SameSite transport policy are HTTP contract and encoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Startup behavior and fact recovery when instance marks are missing
questions: How does Registry distinguish a genuine first start, where absent marks may be created, from loss of the marks beside an existing or restored store, where recreating them could lower the audit high-water mark or lose the migration closure?
How does Registry distinguish first start from deletion or loss of the marks, so it does not reset the audit counter or migration closure?
May a restored nonempty store start when its external instance marks are absent, and if so how are lost sequence and migration-closure facts recovered?

quotes:
The instance marks there (A15) are made at the first start; marks that cannot be read fail
   the start.

the instance marks are not replaced, so
   numbering continues above every number ever written (A15) and a migration
   closure is never lost: at start Registry writes the closure into the store
   when the marks hold it and the store does not, and the import stays closed
   (R0-79).
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats absent marks as a first start and recreates them, potentially losing the audit high-water mark and migration closure; another refuses to start whenever an existing store lacks its marks, which the owner notices as either weakened restored state or unavailable Registry.
judgement.why: The rules do not define how startup distinguishes first initialization from loss of the external marks.

topics.topic: Whether an audit sequence number reserved for a failed transaction is skipped, reused, or reconciled
questions: If the marks advance but the audit-entry transaction fails or the process crashes before commit, must the next entry skip the reserved number or reuse it?

What happens when the marks advance but the state change and audit-entry transaction then fails: is the unused number permanently skipped, is the mark rolled back, or must the whole operation stop until the mark and transaction can be reconciled?
After a number is placed in the marks but its audit transaction never commits, is the next entry allowed to skip that number or must the reservation be rolled back or completed?

quotes:
Sequence numbers are never reused (M09): the next entry continues from the
   last number ever written.

Registry records each number in the instance
   marks — a small file in the backup location, apart from the store and the
   backups, which a restore does not replace (A18) — before the entry
   commits; at start it continues from the higher of the store's last number
   and the marks'.

Neither an erasure, a restart nor a restore lowers it, and
   a number lost with a restore is never issued again.
judgement.divergence: One implementation permanently skips a number reserved before a failed commit; another rolls back or reuses that number because it was never written, and the owner notices different audit sequences.
judgement.why: The rules specify pre-commit reservation and restore loss but not the disposition of a reservation whose ordinary transaction never commits.

topics.topic: Whether import acceptance depends on successful immediate backup
questions: Does an import remain accepted when its immediate backup fails, and if so, is the claim that a backup holding it exists withdrawn?
Is a successful checked backup required before the import is reported accepted, or is the backup merely attempted after the already-accepted import?
What is the result of a successful import whose immediate backup run fails?

quotes:
Right after it Registry makes a backup
   run outside the daily schedule (A18), so a backup holding the import
   exists.

A backup that fails the
   check is deleted and counts as failed.

A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file, writes a
   diagnostic that names the failure and no value (A17), and is tried again at
   the next run; Registry keeps serving.
judgement.why: The import rule guarantees that the immediate run leaves a backup holding the import, while the backup rules allow that run to fail, leave no backup, and keep Registry serving.

topics.topic: Which confirmation submissions consume the pending confirmation
questions: After session and CSRF checks pass, does any submitted confirmation value consume the session's pending confirmation, or only the correct pending one when its action, target and inputs fail a later binding check?
Does any submitted invalid or random confirmation value consume the session's actual pending confirmation, or only a value that matches that pending one but is bound to the wrong action or inputs?
Does any confirmation submission that passes session and CSRF checks consume the session’s pending confirmation, or only a submission presenting that pending one-time value?

quotes:
A submission becomes the first one when it
   passes the owner session and CSRF checks (A04 rule 6, stage 1): one refused
   before them leaves the value unused; from there on, whatever the answer —
   a value bound to another action included — the value is used up.
judgement.divergence: One implementation consumes the pending confirmation after any confirmation submission that passes session and CSRF checks, even with a random value; another consumes it only when the submitted value equals the pending one, which the owner or an attacker notices through whether the legitimate confirmation remains usable.
judgement.why: The text does not say whether “the value” means the submitted value or the session's pending matching value.

topics.topic: Boundary between safe caller-data arguments and caller-controlled interpreted syntax
questions: What backend contract or verification demonstrates that lowering never turns a caller value into syntax, especially if a backend uses interpolation, escaping or generated command text instead of bound parameters?
Does A21 prohibit passing caller data as a bound query or command argument, or only prohibit caller data from controlling interpreted structure?

quotes:
A value a caller gives only ever fills a value place of a query or command
   whose structure the release fixes; it never becomes an identifier, an
   operator or syntax.

How the store's
   backend lowers this is the backend's.

injection_interpreted_input: no input becomes query, command, template or
     other interpreted structure;
judgement.why: Caller data may be passed as a value argument, while the fixed interpreted structure may never be controlled by that data; the backend may choose its lowering only within that rule.

topics.topic: Create-replay recognition point and precedence over lifecycle or eligibility checks
questions: Does a recognized create replay bypass lifecycle and customer-eligibility checks after stages 1–4, or must it pass every stage including stage 6?
At what point is an existing request id recognised as a repeat, and which lifecycle or conflict checks run before that repeat is answered?

quotes:
A repeat passes stages (1) to (4) of A04 rule 6 like any call — rights,
   the session's set, the existence of its project, its values, a publish's
   type among them (A22) — and, for 'add a room' and 'publish an artifact
   pointer', the check that its project is not archived (R0-17, R0-88). No
   other check of stage (6) is made again for a repeat: the customer a
   project named may since be restricted, and the repeat still answers the
   project.

Only an action that passes all
   six may be a repeat that changes nothing (A05); a create's repeat is
   recognised as A01 rule 3 says.
judgement.why: A01 allows a recognized replay to bypass remaining stage-six checks, while A04 requires every repeat to pass all six stages.

topics.topic: Mandatory interoperable authenticated-encryption format for backups
questions: Which authenticated-encryption scheme, nonce generation and storage rules, key-digest algorithm, file format and tamper-detection behavior must every release use?
What cryptographic format must every release use so implementations do not silently choose incompatible or unauthenticated encryption?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the interoperable authenticated-encryption format already assigned to State 6.

quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Migration-closure facts stored in instance marks and reconstructed after restore
questions: Which MigrationClosure facts are stored in the instance marks so that a missing store closure can be reconstructed without inventing values?
What closure facts do the instance marks hold, and what exact MigrationClosure is reconstructed after restoring a backup from before the import?

quotes:
Facts, written once: the instant the import succeeded; the acting principal
(the owner, M07); the confirmation id ("Identity formats"); the identity of
the file accepted, as a digest, so the audit can name what was imported
without its values.

the instance marks are not replaced, so
   numbering continues above every number ever written (A15) and a migration
   closure is never lost: at start Registry writes the closure into the store
   when the marks hold it and the store does not, and the import stays closed
   (R0-79).
judgement.divergence: One implementation stores every MigrationClosure fact in the marks and reconstructs the original closure; another stores only a closed flag and must omit or invent the instant, principal, confirmation id, or digest, which the owner notices when the reconstructed closure or audit evidence is read.
judgement.why: The rules require reconstruction from the marks without defining which required closure facts the marks preserve.

topics.topic: Serialization and loser behavior for concurrent import confirmations
questions: What guarantees that two owner sessions cannot both commit different imports concurrently?
Can exactly one concurrent confirmation commit, and what does the losing confirmation observe?

quotes: At confirmation Registry checks again.

An accepted import stores every picked project with its rooms and pointers,
   the Customers it makes, the migration closure (M10) and its one audit entry
   (M09) in one transaction, after recording the closure in the instance
   marks (A15).

While the closure exists, uploading and confirming an import are refused
   (R0-79).
judgement.divergence: One implementation serializes confirmations so exactly one commits and the loser is refused because the closure exists; another lets both transactions observe no closure and commit different imports, which the owner and all consumers notice in production records.
judgement.why: The checks and atomic transaction do not state how concurrent confirmations are ordered or what the losing confirmation receives.

topics.topic: Serialization of concurrent audit allocation and commit ordering
questions: How are unrelated concurrent state changes ordered so that sequence-number allocation and transaction commit cannot occur in opposite orders?
What serialization and crash-safe update rule governs allocation of audit sequence numbers in the external marks?

quotes: for entries e1 written before e2: e1.sequence < e2.sequence

Registry records each number in the instance
   marks — a small file in the backup location, apart from the store and the
   backups, which a restore does not replace (A18) — before the entry
   commits; at start it continues from the higher of the store's last number
   and the marks'.
judgement.divergence: One implementation serializes sequence allocation through commit order; another permits transaction B to commit before transaction A after receiving the higher number, producing sequence order inconsistent with write order, which the owner notices in the audit log.
judgement.why: No rule couples concurrent external-mark allocation to the commit order required by the audit invariant.

topics.topic: Startup behavior when no initialized Registry store exists
questions: May Registry initialise an absent empty store at first start, or must release installation create and version it before Registry starts?
What must startup do when the configured store location contains no initialized Registry store?

quotes:
The store must open for reading and writing and carry the store
   version of the running release; a store of another version, or
   one that does not open, fails the start — bringing a store to a new version
   is a step of the release, not of the start.
judgement.divergence: One implementation initializes and versions an absent store at first startup; another refuses startup until installation has created it, which the owner notices during a new deployment.
judgement.why: The startup rule covers an openable versioned store and failures but leaves initial creation of an absent store undecided.

topics.topic: Verifiable gate completing reconciliation before service access resumes
questions: What evidence or gate establishes that reconciliation is complete before service and agent access resumes?
What verifiable condition prevents service tokens from being enabled before the required post-restore reconciliation is complete?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about enforcing post-restore reconciliation before service access resumes.

precedent.topic: Enforcement of owner-only quarantine until restore reconciliation completes
quotes:
The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so
   no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to
   the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for
   it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before
   the latest date the owner erased by, before configuring the tokens and
   starting it again.

This is the owner's operation (Explicit exclusions: the
   host's administration), and the owner's record is its evidence; Registry,
   which no longer holds those changes, cannot list them, enforce them or
   tell when this is done.
precedent.why: The texts deliberately assign quarantine and reconciliation enforcement to the owner's host procedure and explicitly state that Registry cannot verify completion.

topics.topic: Whether owner-interface reads require CSRF validation
questions: Must owner-interface read requests also carry and validate the session's CSRF value, or is CSRF checked only for state-changing requests?
Do owner-interface reads require the session’s CSRF value, or only state-changing requests?

quotes:
Every operation — read or change, of a service, Kernel or the owner —
   checks in one order, and the first failure is its answer; a stage that
   does not apply to it is skipped, and each check an operation states belongs
   to the stage of its kind: (1) the caller's authentication and its right to
   the operation (A09) — for the owner, a valid owner session, then its CSRF
   value, then a confirmation value where one is asked (A13);
judgement.why: A04 expressly applies the owner-session CSRF check to every owner operation, including reads.

topics.topic: Atomic ordering of publish or withdrawal against project lifecycle changes
questions: How are a publish or withdrawal, especially one by the owner, ordered against concurrent archiving, anonymising or deleting of the project so that a lifecycle check cannot pass before the lifecycle change and commit afterward?

topics.topic: Behavior of older releases for artifact types removed by newer releases
questions: After restoring or rolling back to an older release, may that old release publish or withdraw a type removed by a later release?

topics.topic: Catch-up behavior after a missed scheduled daily backup
questions: If Registry was stopped at yesterday's 03:00 and starts today before 03:00, does it immediately make yesterday's missed backup or wait for today's scheduled run?

topics.topic: Classes of post-backup changes covered by restore reconciliation
questions: Which classes of changes after the backup must be replayed or reconciled before normal service resumes?

topics.topic: Closed lists and rejection rules for caller-controlled structural selectors
questions: Which caller-controlled values are structural selectors, what is each selector's closed list, and must an unrecognized selector be refused before any query or command is built?

topics.topic: Digest algorithm and byte representation used to identify an import file
questions: What digest algorithm and byte representation identify the uploaded file and bind the confirmation and migration closure to it?

topics.topic: Effect of a successful owner sign-in on existing owner sessions
questions: How do existing owner sessions change when the owner signs in successfully again?

topics.topic: Equality and canonicalization rules for confirmation-bound inputs
questions: By what equality rule are the submitted inputs compared with the inputs bound to the confirmation, including blank versus absent optional values, ordering, and equivalent serializations?

topics.topic: Exact backup-retention boundary and enforcement of the 30-day erasure limit
questions: At exactly 30 days of age is a backup retained or deleted, and how can the stated at-most-30-day erasure bound hold with only one daily deletion run?

topics.topic: Handling imported project display names that violate naming rules
questions: Must the owner provide a replacement display name for an imported project whose source name violates the naming rule, even though Registry does not inspect names semantically?

topics.topic: Imported facts displayed and bound into the import confirmation
questions: Which imported facts must be displayed and bound into the confirmation, particularly the object's address, kind and characteristics and the kept source instants?

topics.topic: Isolation, ownership, retrieval, and cleanup rules for materialized uploaded files
questions: If uploaded files are materialised outside memory, what isolation, ownership, retrieval and cleanup rules make the files_artifacts review complete?

topics.topic: Meaning and mutability of the written-once OwnerSession expiry fact
questions: What exactly is the written-once expiry fact: the absolute eight-hour deadline, the current effective expiry, or another value, and is any expiry value updated after requests?

topics.topic: Permitted import references to rooms and the required integrity graph
questions: Which record kinds may name a room, and what exact referential-integrity graph must the import validate?

topics.topic: Representation and accepted encodings for the minimum-length secret
questions: What representation is validated for the 32-byte minimum, and which textual encodings are accepted in configuration?

topics.topic: Same-day retry policy for a failed daily backup
questions: May a restart later on the same UTC day retry a failed run, or is the next attempt always on the next day?

topics.topic: Security-review evidence and status after the A19 change
questions: Has the changed A19 been re-reviewed for both affected categories, and what are their current evidence and outcome?

topics.topic: Validity of concurrency-review status while concurrency decisions remain open
questions: Can the concurrency review remain PERFORMED before audit-number allocation, migration-mark commit, and concurrent import confirmation behavior are closed?

topics.topic: Visibility and handling of create request-id collisions across projects or sessions
questions: When Kernel reuses a request id carried by a Room or ArtifactPointer belonging to another project or session, may the existing record be returned, or must the collision be hidden?

questions: Does the post-import backup count as that day’s backup and suppress the scheduled or catch-up daily run?

questions: Can the restored instance create a fresh 30-day backup containing personal data that should already have been erased before the owner finishes reconciliation?

topics.topic: Whether confirmation expiry is inclusive at exactly ten minutes
questions: Is a confirmation accepted when now equals shown_at plus exactly 10 minutes?

topics.topic: Whether invalid unpicked import records are validated and may block confirmation
questions: Are malformed records and conflicts outside the picked projects reported and allowed to block confirmation?

topics.topic: Whether sign-in requests require CSRF protection and what it binds to
